title: A good name (Avot 4:13)
hookLine: three crowns, Torah, priesthood and kingship, and the crown of a good name above them all
tomorrow: can you learn it just as well from home? Rabbi Nehorai says no.

lines: A TITLE. A DIPLOMA. A SEAT.
cards: A diploma on a wall, a title in an email signature, a seat at the head of the table. All crowns, of a kind. Rabbi Shimon counts three big ones: the crown of Torah, the crown of priesthood, the crown of kingship.
And then he names a fourth, and says it rises above all three. Which one can anyone wear? The one nobody hands you.

teach.b: Here's Rabbi Shimon, in plain words. There are three crowns: Torah, priesthood and kingship.

teach.h: A GOOD NAME RISES ABOVE THEM.
teach.b: But the crown of a good name rises above them all. Priesthood came by birth. Kingship came by line or by power.
Torah, learning, comes by long work. A good name comes from none of those. It's built by how you treat people when it costs you something, and it can't be inherited or bought.
That's why it rises above the rest: the other crowns are worn on the head, and this one is worn in other people's mouths.
Now the week, because a good name is made of it. Only one judges alone: ask a second pair of eyes. Poor or rich: the thin weeks build the habit.
Less business: cut on purpose. Make an advocate: each good deed speaks for you. For heaven's sake endures: name what the gathering is for.
And honor the student: guard the dignity of the newest person in the room. Six sayings.
Put them together and you get a good name.

how: In Jewish tradition a person's good name, shem tov, is guarded closely, and the laws against gossip and shaming in public are part of protecting other people's names, too.

o: a name earned by how you treat people
a well-known name that many people know
a lucky name given at birth by your parents

games.q: the four crowns — tap the pairs.
p: came by line or by power
the crown of a good name

s: a good name is the fourth crown, and it rises above the other three
Rabbi Shimon names three crowns, then the crown of a good name above them.
a good name means being well-known or well known
it's built by how you treat people, not by how many know you.

games.q: a classmate offers you the answers to a test nobody would ever find out about. in Rabbi Shimon's terms, what's at stake?
o: the crown of a good name, which is built by what you do when nobody's checking.
nothing, since a good name only depends on what other people find out.
the crown of Torah, since tests are a kind of learning.
games.why: the other crowns can be handed down or earned by study. a good name is made of how you act, seen or unseen.

practice: Say your own full name out loud, once, slowly, as if someone were introducing you to a room. Then sit with what you'd want the room to hear right after it: one plain thing about how you treat people.

wordCard.voice: A good name. Rabbi Shimon: three crowns, Torah, priesthood and kingship, and the crown of a good name above them all.

orig.note: Hebrew: the crown of a good name. keter is crown; shem tov, a good name.

carryVoice: Keep this one: a good name, the crown nobody can hand you. A week of chapter four, thirty-six of sixty.
